A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MaskSub research despite the changed title and terminology. All 17 pages of v2 and 19 pages of v3, including Appendices A and B, provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original training, finetuning, transfer-learning, robustness, and ablation results, including ImageNet experiments, BERT/GLUE evaluation, and CLIP pretraining.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds comparison results, IN-C robustness evaluation, and further ablations.

M1.justification: The default shared-network procedure, equal-weight supervised and distillation losses, stop-gradient, and DropSub/PathSub variants remain unchanged. Appendix Table A.9 adds limited procedural variants using multiple masked sub-branches and additional branch-specific photometric augmentation. Renaming and the gradient-accumulation disclosure do not establish changes to the default algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds IN-C to the image-robustness evaluation in Table A.4. The other datasets and domains are retained. BERT/GLUE, CLIP pretraining, ADE-20k segmentation, and COCO detection were already evaluated in v2; moving segmentation into the main text does not add coverage.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds RSB + SD-dropout and RSB + PS-KD comparisons for ResNet101 and ResNet152, supplementing the earlier comparisons using weaker recipes. Other comparator sets remain unchanged, including the MAE-finetuning comparison moved from v2 Table 9 to v3 Table A.2.

E3.justification: New experiments compare branch counts and photometric augmentations using ViT-B/16 with 400-epoch DeiT-III training, and evaluate self-distillation comparators with RSB. Figure A.1 adds convergence evaluation against GPU-day budgets. The existing training settings in Tables B.1 and B.2 are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of whether multiple sub-branches, color jitter, or Gaussian blur improve MaskSub (Table A.9), extends robustness evaluation with IN-C, and adds budget-based convergence analysis (Figure A.1). Existing KD-loss, masking-ratio, loss-weight, drop-regularization, and robustness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independent runs with different seeds and the same mean-and-standard-deviation results for the corresponding analyses. v2 Tables A.9–A.12 become v3 Tables A.10–A.13. No new uncertainty estimation practice, run-count increase, or significance test is reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds RSB-based comparator scores, IN-C results, and budget-based curves. Table A.9 reports 84.03 and 83.76 accuracy with two and three sub-branches, 84.18 with color jitter, and 84.05 with blur, versus 84.10 for standard MaskSub. Table A.4 adds, for example, ViT-B IN-C scores of 38.1 without and 36.9 with MaskSub. Retained headline benchmark accuracies are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), the loss construction, and the underlying mathematical reasoning remain unchanged. The expanded discussion of distillation difficulty is conceptual explanation; neither version adds formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain stable: MaskSub enables strong masking during supervised learning, preserves or improves convergence, and improves performance across training recipes. Highlighting BERT in the later abstract and introduction promotes evidence already present in v2 rather than introducing a new scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new ablations as favoring a single sub-branch and additional color jitter. Section 4 changes the characterization of competing self-distillation methods from incompatible with strong recipes to less effective. It also removes v2's one-sixth-cost claim against GradAug while retaining the underlying 8.6 versus 23.4 GPU-day results.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 newly explains separate backward passes with PyTorch gradient accumulation to release main-branch memory before sub-branch computation. Section 4.2 explicitly identifies BEiTv2 block masking. These are additional disclosures, not established changes to earlier experiments. Hardware, recipe tables, and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion distinguishing MaskSub from UDA's semi-supervised consistency training, expands the comparison with MAE/SupMAE, and cites three additional distillation studies to motivate teacher difficulty. All 68 earlier references are retained; four works are added.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, main-model/sub-model terminology becomes main-branch/sub-branch, and prose is edited throughout. Related-work and implementation explanations expand, while self-distillation receives its own experimental subsection. The overall introduction–method–experiments–conclusion narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Visual organization is extensively revised: Figure 1 moves earlier, Figure 3 becomes Figure 2d, and Figure A.1 is added. Table 2 gains a cost column; segmentation and MAE comparisons move between the main text and appendix; transfer and GLUE tables are resized; and appendix tables are broadly reformatted. v3 Table 7 incorrectly labels both CIFAR columns CIFAR100, although the text and appendix preserve their identities.

improvement.justification: The RSB-based self-distillation comparisons improve comparability, while IN-C evaluation and additional ablations strengthen validation of the existing method. The memory-management explanation also improves reproducibility. These gains are incremental because most evidence was already present in v2. The new CIFAR column-label error and missing uncertainty for the small new ablation differences limit the overall improvement.
